title: Harden SSE parser state machine and terminal delimiter handling
author: Lina Ortega
release_notes: Fix: make SSE event framing deterministic under concurrent chunking; avoids partial-JSON corruption and duplicate/empty events. Adds observability and opt-in rollout flag.
description:
Context: We observed rare customer reports and internal canaries where SSE streams emitted duplicate empty events or yielded partial/invalid JSON in downstream consumers. Root cause: the compatibility layer's streaming parser aggressively consumed terminal delimiters (\n\n) and normalized chunk boundaries in a way that could conflate an event terminator with the start of the next event when upstream chunking split a single logical event across TCP frames. This manifested under high-concurrency and small-chunk workloads (low MTU / proxy slicing) and was amplified by earlier retry/replay logic.

Goal: Make the SSE parser state machine deterministic and lossless for the OpenAI-compatible streaming surface: 1) never drop or merge delimiter tokens incorrectly; 2) recover partial JSON payloads deterministically when they arrive across multiple chunks; 3) add lightweight sequence checks and observability to diagnose reassembly failures.

What I changed: 1) Rewrote the parser state machine to explicitly model: STREAM_IDLE, IN_EVENT, IN_DATA_LINE, IN_REMAINDER. The new transitions defer consuming a terminal double-newline until we've validated whether the next bytes constitute a valid event head. 2) Introduced an in-stream sequence marker (compat-only header injection when allowed by upstream) and CRC8 on reassembled event payloads to detect reorder/corruption during replay. Sequence and CRC are optional and disabled by default; they are enabled under the new feature-flag for gradual rollout. 3) Added a max_event_size guard and safe backpressure path: when an event exceeds config.max_event_size we emit a new metric and drop parsing state to avoid unbounded memory growth (previous code could hang the streaming goroutine). 4) Normalized handling for CRLF and LF-only endpoints: parser now canonicalizes newline semantics before tokenization to avoid platform-specific delimiter bugs. 5) Added extensive unit and integration tests: deterministic reassembly harness, fuzz cases (random chunk boundaries), and a small end-to-end runner that simulates small-fragment proxies. 6) Added observability: sse.reassembly.attempts, sse.reassembly.failures, sse.partial_json.recoveries, sse.oversize_events. 7) Documentation: sse/framing.md describing semantics, rollout plan, and backport guidance.

Testing: Added 18 new unit tests and 6 integration scenarios. Reproduced customer canary where a 3KB JSON event was split into 9 340-byte chunks and previously resulted in an invalid event being delivered ~1% of the time. All new tests pass locally and on CI. One flaky integration test in the first CI run (integration/stream_replay) failed intermittently; re-ran the job after adding a short jitter to the test harness and it stabilized.

Rollout plan: Feature gated under openai.sse.strict_reassembly. Default for hosted customers remains unchanged for 48 hours post-merge; we will enable for canary customers and monitor the new metrics for 72 hours before turning on by default. Backport to the 2026-02 release branch planned after canary validation.

Notes and non-goals: This PR focuses on surface-level reassembly and delimiter correctness for OpenAI-compatible SSE. It does not change how function/tool calling payloads are typed or introduce new semantic framing for function call sentinels; those are follow-ups tracked in ENG-5020.

Checklist:
- [x] Parser state machine rewrite
- [x] Deterministic partial JSON reassembly with CRC check
- [x] New metrics and docs
- [x] Unit + integration + fuzz tests
- [x] Feature-flagged rollout

Related: customer report SUP-1128, ENG-4921 (streaming stability epic).
